Messages via mt_inform() (silent unless options(mortensor.verbose = TRUE)). data.table inside package: column names used non-standard evaluation go utils::globalVariables() R/mortensor-package.R. Randomness: functions simulate take seed = NULL use with_seed(); parallel code uses parallel L’Ecuyer streams. title: Backtesting and scores
text: Deaths populations England sex deprivation quintile, 2001-2019 (ONS). Three models, chosen examples: random walk drift per age (rwd()): log rate continues average change past. standard benchmark forecasting: model beat adds little; Lee-Carter (lee_carter()), one model per stratum; Li-Lee (li_lee(common_by = "sex")), quintiles sex pooled around common trend.
code: library(mortensor) library(data.table) x <- mt_data(deaths = ons_data, population = ons_data, by = c("sex", "imd_decile"), age = "age_group",              value = c(deaths = "all_causes", population = "population")) x <- mt_as_exposure(x, type = "midyear") x <- mt_group_levels(x, "imd_decile", function(d) paste0("Q", ceiling(as.numeric(d) / 2)), name = "quintile") models <- list("random walk" = rwd(), "Lee-Carter" = lee_carter(), "Li-Lee" = li_lee(common_by = "sex"))

title: Backtesting and scores
text: continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares whole forecast distribution observed value: integral squared difference forecast’s cumulative distribution step observed value (Gneiting Raftery 2007). figure shades difference two curves; squared summed axis, gives CRPS:  forecast puts probability close observed value small area. CRPS punishes distribution target one wider necessary. forecast without uncertainty equals absolute error, unit forecast quantity: log death rates, CRPS 0.05 means errors roughly 5% rate; life expectancy years. Lower better. weighted interval score (WIS, Bracher et al. 2021) approximates CRPS central intervals; reported well ranks models way.

title: Bayesian age-period-cohort models with bamp

text: code writes two CSV files (semicolon-separated, many European exports). data, start files.
code: set.seed(42) ages <- c("unter 1 Jahr", "1 bis unter 5 Jahre", paste(seq(5, 85, 5), "bis unter", seq(10, 90, 5), "Jahre"),           "90 Jahre und mehr") lo <- c(0, 1, seq(5, 90, 5)) g <- CJ(Jahr = 2005:2022, Geschlecht = 1:2, Quintil = 1:5, k = seq_along(ages)) g[, Altersgruppe := ages[k]] g[, bev := round(4e4 * exp(-lo[k] / 45) * (1 + 0.1 * (Quintil == 1)))] g[, rate := exp(-10.1 + 0.09 * (lo[k] + 2) + 0.3 * (Geschlecht == 1) + 0.12 * (5 - Quintil) - 0.015 * (Jahr - 2005))] g[k == 1, rate := 0.004] g[Jahr %in% 2020:2022, rate := rate * 1.12]                 # pandemic years g[, Gestorbene := rpois(.N, bev * pmin(rate, 0.7))] deaths <- g[, .(Jahr, Geschlecht, Quintil, Altersgruppe,                 Gestorbene = ifelse(Gestorbene == 0, "-", ifelse(Gestorbene < 3, ".", Gestorbene)))] totals <- g[, .(Altersgruppe = "Insgesamt", Gestorbene = as.character(sum(Gestorbene))),             by = .(Jahr, Geschlecht, Quintil)] deaths <- rbind(deaths, totals) pop <- g[, .(Stichtag = Jahr, Geschlecht, Quintil, Altersgruppe, Bevoelkerung = bev)] pop <- rbind(pop[Stichtag == 2005][, Stichtag := 2004], pop)   # 31 December of the year before f_deaths <- file.path(tempdir(), "gestorbene.csv") f_pop <- file.path(tempdir(), "bevoelkerung.csv") fwrite(deaths, f_deaths, sep = ";") fwrite(pop, f_pop, sep = ";")

title: Smoothing death rates
text: mt_smooth() smooths one three directions: age, year separately (Poisson P-splines): removes noise neighbouring ages, keeps every year observed; time, age separately (Whittaker smoothing log rates): removes year--year variation, keeps age pattern every year; age-period surface (additive model tensor-product spline te(age, year), package mgcv): .  points observed rates women Q1. Smoothing age leaves almost year--year variation, 5-year age groups neighbouring ages already agree closely; matters single years age sparse data (small areas, causes death). Smoothing time surface remove year--year variation keep trend, including end decline 2011. surface follows last years little closely.
code: sm <- list("over age" = mt_smooth(x),            "over time" = mt_smooth(x, along = "period", method = "whittaker"),            "age-period surface" = mt_smooth(x, dims = 2, method = "gam")) mt_plot_smooth(x, sm, ages = c("45-49", "65-69", "85-89"), strata = "female.Q1")

Small values mean annual variation removed. age, dispersion 1: 20 age groups per year spline stays close points. time surface, observed deaths vary twice much Poisson noise around trend: years differ chance, smoothing treats year effects noise. Whether right depends question. trend forecast continues, usually .

text: Wrapper around bamp package (Schmid Held 2007): binomial likelihood deaths given exposures, logit link, random walk priors first second order age, period cohort effects, optional overdispersion, MCMC four chains. title: mortensor: flexible mortality forecasting across data granularities — mortensor-package
text: Data: mt_data() stores deaths, exposures populations observed age period resolution (age_groups(), single_ages(), single_years(), parse_age_labels()); as_mt_data() mt_from_hmd() read Human Mortality Database data; mt_validate() checks plausibility; mt_example() simulates data known truth. Harmonisation: mt_regroup() aggregates exactly, mt_ungroup() estimates single-year data penalized composite link model, mt_smooth() smooths rates; mt_prep() bundles steps backtests refit every training window. Models: rwd(), lee_carter(), tucker3(), arima_series(), ets_series(), hyndman_ullah(), stmomo(), li_lee(), product_ratio(), apc_bayes() (package bamp), cause_shares() coherent multi-cause forecasts ensemble(), fitted mt_fit() (optionally tuned tuned()) forecast mt_forecast() simulated paths (mt_draws). Hierarchies: mt_hierarchy() describes crossed nested strata (example sex x region x deprivation quintile totals), mt_aggregate_strata() adds aggregates, mt_reconcile() reconciled() make forecasts add draw draw, mt_order_strata() imposes orderings. Wrappers model: ensemble(), reconciled(), recalibrated() (spread fitted recent forecast errors), anchored() (jump-observed level), bootstrapped() tuned(). Evaluation: mt_backtest() mt_score(), rates, life expectancy age-standardised rates. past: mt_observed(), mt_contrast() mt_inequality(). Derived quantities plots: life_table(), life_expectancy(), mt_deaths(), mt_plot_forecast() mt_plot_*() functions. Decomposition: mt_decompose() splits differences life expectancy summaries age, cause subgroup composition, observed data, forecasts .
